summary: South Mountain lookout on the Washington/Frederick line, built 1934 from a reused 60-ft tower; removed in 2006 and replaced by a fenced communications site.

access.note: Summit is a chain-link fenced communications compound; no source describes visitor access inside it

corrections.why: 24.4 m is the 80-foot figure from the 1934 plan; the Maryland DNR 2007 inventory records the original tower at 91 feet, or 27.7 m

resolved_conflicts.explanation: Sources give 80 feet (1934 plan), 110 feet to the apex (1939 Coast and Geodetic Survey description) and 91 feet (DNR 2007). The story and facts use the owner's 91-foot record.
DNR places the site on the Washington/Frederick county line; the eastern site heading says Frederick County; a 1956 clipping says Washington County.

sources.title: Forestry Towers and Forestry Tower Properties: A Resource Document
Lamb's Knoll (newspaper clippings and survey notes)

notes_for_editor: Height is the main conflict: 80 ft (1934 plan), 110 ft (1939 NGS apex) and 91 ft (DNR 2007, owner's record); the brief's 24.4 m is the 80-ft plan. Removal in 2006 is confirmed by DNR and Willhite. Staffing dates found are 1942 and a 1956 seasonal note only; no source found gives the end of staffing. A search summary claimed closure in the 1980s and staffing through the late 1940s; no fetched page confirmed it, so it is left out. Willhite describes the 1942 towerman as the lookout person and the 0.1 side-trail figure without a unit.
